1.title: Subject of the Act
paragraphs: Art. 1. This Act regulates the legal status of the notary and of the Notary Chamber, the organisation of notarial activity and the notarial fees.

2.title: Notary
paragraphs: Art. 2. (1) A notary is a person to whom the state assigns the performance of the notarial acts provided for by law.
(2) Only a person entered in the register of the Notary Chamber can be a notary.
(3) The notary performs the notarial acts and the other acts provided for by law personally.

3.title: District
paragraphs: Art. 3. The district of a notary coincides with the district of the respective district court.

4.title: Notary Chamber
paragraphs: Art. 4. (1) A Notary Chamber is established. All notaries are members of the Notary Chamber by law.
(2) The Notary Chamber is a legal entity with its seat in Sofia.

(3) To support the activity of the Notary Chamber and of the notaries, a notarial college is established in the judicial area of each court of appeal. A separate college is established for Sofia city.
(4) The statute and the functions of the notarial colleges are set in the statute of the Notary Chamber.

5.title: Register of the Notary Chamber
paragraphs: Art. 5. The Notary Chamber keeps a register. The notaries, the assistant notaries and the related circumstances provided for by law are entered in the register.

6.title: Duty to apply for entry
paragraphs: Art. 6. A person who must by law declare circumstances subject to entry in the register under Art. 5, or present documents, must do so within 7 days of the occurrence of the circumstance, unless the law sets another term.

7.title: Publicity of the register
paragraphs: Art. 7. Everyone has the right to inspect the register of the Notary Chamber and to receive an extract from it.

8.title: Requirements
paragraphs: Art. 8. (1) A natural person with capacity, aged up to 60, who is a citizen of Bulgaria, of a Member State of the European Union, of a State party to the Agreement on the European Economic Area or of the Swiss Confederation, may acquire capacity as a notary if the person:
1. has a higher education in law;
2. has acquired legal capacity under the Judiciary Act;
3. has three years of experience;
4. has not been sentenced to imprisonment for an intentional crime, even if rehabilitated;
5. has not been deprived of capacity as a notary;
6. has not been deprived of the right to practise as a lawyer or to carry out commercial activity;
7. is not in insolvency proceedings, is not an insolvent person whose rights were not restored, and has not been convicted of bankruptcy;
8. is entered in the register under Art. 5.

(2) The experience under para. 1, item 3 includes service as a judge, prosecutor, investigator, lawyer, arbitrator, junior judge, junior prosecutor, junior investigator, judicial assistant at the Supreme Court of Cassation or the Supreme Administrative Court, prosecutor's assistant, state or private bailiff, assistant private bailiff, notary, registration judge, assistant notary, researcher in law, judicial inspector, legislative expert or expert in the judiciary, legal adviser or legal expert in state or municipal administration, investigating police officer with a law degree, investigating customs inspector, and the internship under Art. 164(9) of the Judiciary Act.

(3) The experience under para. 1, item 3 also includes three years of experience that counts as legal experience under the law of the Member State of the European Union, the State party to the Agreement on the European Economic Area or the Swiss Confederation where it was acquired.

9.title: Incompatibility
paragraphs: Art. 9. (1) A notary may not at the same time:
1. be a member of Parliament, a minister, a mayor or a municipal councillor;
2. hold a position in a state or municipal body;
3. work under an employment relationship;
4. practise as a lawyer;
5. carry out commercial activity, be a manager, or take part in supervisory, management or control bodies of commercial companies or cooperatives.
(2) When the activity under para. 1, item 1 ends, the notary's capacity is restored under the conditions of Art. 39.

10.title: Opening of places for notaries. Competition
paragraphs: Art. 10. (1) The places for notaries in a district may not be fewer than two. One place for a notary is opened for every 10,000 inhabitants of a district.

(2) Vacant places for notaries are filled through a competition announced by order of the Minister of Justice. The Council of Notaries gives its opinion within 14 days. The Minister of Justice may also announce a competition on a proposal of the Council of Notaries.
(3) The order under para. 2 is communicated in writing to the Notary Chamber. The order that has entered into force is published in the State Gazette.

(4) When more notaries than those under para. 1 are needed, the Minister of Justice may, on his own initiative or on a proposal of the Council of Notaries, open additional places for notaries in the district.
(5) The Minister of Justice permits the move of a notary entered in the register of the Notary Chamber to another judicial district.

11.title: Application procedure
paragraphs: Art. 11. (1) Within one month of the publication of the order under Art. 10(2), the candidates submit a written application to the Minister of Justice to take part in the competition. The application contains the name, the personal number (for a Bulgarian citizen) or the date and place of birth (for a citizen of another Member State, an EEA State or Switzerland), the address and the profession, and the order of the judicial districts for which the candidate applies. In one competition a candidate may name up to three judicial districts.

(2) The application is accompanied by documents for the state fee paid, birth, identity, a completed higher education in law and legal capacity under the Judiciary Act (if the certificate of legal capacity was issued before 1 March 2011), length of service and place of work, a criminal record certificate if the candidate is not a Bulgarian citizen, a declaration under Art. 8, items 5, 6 and 7, and a medical certificate.
(3) When the candidate completed the law education abroad, the application is accompanied by a copy of the diploma and a document certifying that the diploma is recognised in Bulgaria.

(4) When the three years of legal experience were acquired under the law of another Member State, an EEA State or Switzerland, the application is accompanied by documents proving this experience and an extract from the rules of that State that recognise the experience as legal experience.
(5) When there are no candidates for all places in a district, the term is extended by one month. In this case persons over 60 may also apply for that district.

12.title: Competition for notaries
paragraphs: Art. 12. (1) The conditions and the procedure of the competition are set by an ordinance of the Minister of Justice after agreement with the Council of Notaries.

(2) The competition is held by a commission composed of: a chair, a representative of the Ministry of Justice appointed by the Minister; and as members a judge of the Supreme Court of Cassation appointed by its President, two notaries appointed by the Council of Notaries, and a habilitated lecturer in civil law appointed by the Minister of Justice.

(3) The commission sends the protocol with the results to the Minister of Justice, who within 14 days issues an order for entry in the register of the Notary Chamber of the candidate ranked for the district.

(4) The order under para. 3 is announced to the candidates for the district and to the Council of Notaries under Art. 18a(10) of the Administrative Procedure Code. It may be appealed before the Administrative Court of Sofia Region under the Administrative Procedure Code.
(5) The Ministry of Justice collects a state fee for the competition in an amount set by a tariff approved by the Council of Ministers.

13.title: Notary office
paragraphs: Art. 13. (1) After the order for entry enters into force, the candidate notary must provide a notary office, which may also be done together with other candidates or acting notaries from the same district.
(2) The notary office must have two or more functionally connected rooms, which must house the notary's chancery and official archive.

(3) A notary may have only one notary office in the notary's district. The office must meet conditions that guarantee the safekeeping of the archive and the precise performance of the notary's professional duties.

14.title: Entry in the register of the Notary Chamber
paragraphs: Art. 14. (1) Entry in the register of the Notary Chamber is made by decision of the Council of Notaries.
(2) For the entry of a notary in the register:
1. the order of the Minister of Justice for entry must have entered into force;
2. a written declaration that the obstacles under Art. 9 do not exist must be presented;
3. the address of the notary office must be stated and the requirements of Art. 13(2) and (3) must be met;

4. a document for a real right in the notary office or an entered lease contract must be presented, together with a declaration on the origin of the funds invested in the office, on a form approved by the Minister of Justice;
5. a document for the insurance under Art. 30 must be presented;
6. a specimen of the seal approved by the Minister of Justice must be presented;
7. a specimen of the notary's signature must be presented.
(3) For the entry of an assistant notary, the requirements of para. 2, items 1, 2, 5 and 7 are sufficient.

(4) The request for entry and the fulfilment of the requirements of paras. 2 and 3 must be made within two months of the entry into force of the order. For a place not taken, the Minister of Justice issues an order for entry of the next ranked candidate.

(5) Within one month of the request for entry, the Council of Notaries inspects the candidate's notary office for compliance with Art. 13(2) and (3). A protocol of the findings is attached to the request.

15.title: Oath
paragraphs: Art. 15. (1) After the decision under Art. 14(1), the candidate, if he has not done so before, takes the following oath before the Council of Notaries: "I swear to observe strictly the Constitution and the laws of the Republic of Bulgaria, to perform my professional duties honestly, conscientiously and impartially, to be worthy of the trust and respect that the profession requires, to contribute to the prestige of the profession, and to keep professional secrecy, always remembering that I answer to the law for everything. I have sworn!"
(2) After the oath, an oath sheet is signed.
(3) The entry in the register is made after the oath sheet is signed.

16.title: Circumstances entered in the register
paragraphs: Art. 16. (1) The register contains:
1. the district;
2. the name and personal number of the notary or the assistant notary;
3. the address of the notary office;
4. the term of office of the assistant notary, including when substituting;
5. the name and seat of the insurer and the sum insured;
6. the circumstances under Art. 41, 42 and 46.
(2) The persons entered in the register of the Notary Chamber must apply within 7 days for the entry of changes in the circumstances subject to entry.

17.title: Independence
paragraphs: Art. 17. (1) The notary is independent and, in performing his functions, is subject only to the law.
(2) When a notary is detained or charged with a publicly prosecuted crime, the Minister of Justice and the Council of Notaries are informed.

18.title: Assistance and respect
paragraphs: Art. 18. The notary is owed assistance and respect in the performance of his functions.

19.title: Access to documents
paragraphs: Art. 19. (1) The notary has free access to the court and administrative offices, may consult cases and files, may ask for copies, transcripts and documents, and receives information and certificates with priority.

(2) The notary has access to the National Database "Population" maintained by the Ministry of Regional Development and Public Works, and to the National Automated Information Fund for Bulgarian Identity Documents – "National Register of Bulgarian Identity Documents", under conditions and a procedure set by an act of the Council of Ministers.

20.title: Meeting alone
paragraphs: Art. 20. In performing his official functions, the notary meets alone with the person who asked for his assistance, unless that person wishes others to be present.

21.title: Inviolability of the official archive
paragraphs: Art. 21. (1) The official archive of the notary is inviolable, and nobody has the right of access to it without the notary's consent, except in the cases provided for by law.
(2) A person who obtained access to the official archive must keep the official secret under the conditions set for the notary, and must inform the notary of the actions taken with the archive.

22.title: Other activities of the notary
paragraphs: Art. 22. If the parties instruct him, the notary may, in connection with notarial proceedings, prepare and check draft documents, give oral and written consultations, mediate to clarify the will of the parties, make inquiries, obtain documents and papers, and act as executor of a will or as manager of property.

23.title: Duty to assist
paragraphs: Art. 23. The notary considers all requests for assistance addressed to him, unless he has an interest in the requested act or is in special relations with the party that give reasonable doubt about his impartiality.

24.title: Impartiality
paragraphs: Art. 24. In performing his official functions, the notary may not take sides.

25.title: Protection of the rights and interests of the parties
paragraphs: Art. 25. (1) The notary must protect the rights and interests of the parties, guide them, clarify their will and the facts, inform them clearly and unambiguously of the legal consequences, and not allow omissions or delays in the work that could harm their rights.
(2) Before drawing up the act, the notary checks whether a security measure has been imposed under the Act on the Forfeiture of Illegally Acquired Assets.
(3) In all notarial certifications connected with the creation, change or termination of rights in real estate, the notary must make an inquiry in the databases and funds under Art. 19(2).
(4) (Repealed.)

(5) The notary presents the acts subject to entry to the registry office on the day they are performed. A marriage contract in the cases of Art. 39(3) of the Family Code is presented for entry on receipt of the certificate of civil marriage. Before the entry, the notary may not give the parties a copy of the act subject to entry.
(6) Acts subject to entry in another judicial district are sent to the registry offices officially on the order of the registration judge. The costs of sending are borne by the parties.
(7) (Repealed.)
(8) In dispositions, the parties must present to the notary a declaration on citizenship and marital status on a form approved by the Minister of Justice.

(9) In transactions for value that create, transfer, change or end real rights in real estate, the participants in the notarial proceedings declare in the act that the sum stated in it is the payment actually agreed under the transaction.
(10) Payments under para. 9 totalling more than 10,000 leva are made through a special bank account of the notary or through a bank account in a bank chosen by the parties.

26.title: Professional secrecy
paragraphs: Art. 26. (1) The notary must keep professional secrecy about the circumstances that became known to him in connection with his work, and may not use them for his own or another person's benefit.
(2) The duties under para. 1 also apply to the time when the notary does not perform his functions or his activity has ended.

27.title: Continuity of activity
paragraphs: Art. 27. The Minister of Justice sets the working hours of notary offices and the conditions under which they may be temporarily closed.

28.title: Official archive
paragraphs: Art. 28. (1) The notary keeps his own official archive. The conditions and procedure for keeping the archive are set by an ordinance of the Minister of Justice after agreement with the Council of Notaries.
(2) The official archive contains:
1. notarial registers and books;
2. notarial case files;
3. other documents;
4. the notary's seal.

(3) Case files and documents leave the notary office only on a written order (ruling, order, decree) of a judge or a prosecutor. Copies are handed against signature to an official expressly named in the order.

(4) Originals kept in the official archive may leave the notary office, in the cases of an express order under para. 3, only with the notary personally, and an expert examination may be made only in his presence.
(5) The notary's seal may be seized, or the office sealed, only if the notary has lost capacity.

29.title: Notice to the president of the district court
paragraphs: Art. 29. The notary immediately informs the president of the district court of every change in the location of the notary office and of his official archive.

30.title: Insurance
paragraphs: Art. 30. (1) The notary is insured for the period of his professional activity against the damage that may result from culpable non-performance of his duties and of the duties of the assistant notary and the employees of the office. The minimum and maximum sum insured are set by the Notary Chamber.
(2) Within 7 days of concluding the contract under para. 1, the notary must present a copy of the policy to the Notary Chamber.

31.title: Social insurance
paragraphs: Art. 31. The notary is subject to compulsory social insurance under the conditions and procedure for persons in liberal professions.

32.title: Contributions to the Notary Chamber
paragraphs: Art. 32. The notary makes compulsory contributions to the Notary Chamber under the conditions and procedure of the Chamber's statute and the decisions of the general meeting.

33.title: Accounting
paragraphs: Art. 33. The notary keeps accounts.

34.title: Professional ethics and qualification
paragraphs: Art. 34. (1) The notary must observe professional ethics and protect the prestige of the profession according to the statute of the Notary Chamber.
(2) The notary must introduce to the work, train and guide the assistant notary and his employees.

35.title: Grounds for loss of capacity
paragraphs: Art. 35. A notary loses capacity:
1. on his written request to the Council of Notaries;
2. on death or on being placed under judicial disability;
3. when an obstacle under Art. 8 or an incompatibility under Art. 9 arises;
4. when the disciplinary penalty under Art. 75(1), item 4 is imposed.

36.title: Sealing and inventory of the official archive
paragraphs: Art. 36. (1) When a ground under Art. 35 occurs, the notary may not perform any notarial or other act provided for by law, and the official archive is sealed.
(2) The official archive is sealed and unsealed on the order of the president of the district court, and a protocol with an inventory is drawn up.
(3) The conditions and procedure for sealing, unsealing and handing over the official archive are set by an ordinance of the Minister of Justice after agreement with the Council of Notaries.
(4) Enforcement or acts of non-contentious proceedings in premises entered as a notary office may take place only after the notary's official archive has been handed over.

37.title: Deletion from the register
paragraphs: Art. 37. (1) The Council of Notaries deletes a notary from the register of its own motion by noting in the register:
1. the ground for the loss of capacity;
2. the date and the name of the person to whom the archive was handed over.
(2) The capacity of the notary is lost with the deletion from the register, except in the cases of Art. 35, item 2.
(3) Within three days of the deletion the Council of Notaries informs the Minister of Justice, who may announce a competition if the conditions of Art. 10 are met.

38.title: Notarial acts on the archive received
paragraphs: Art. 38. The notary, or the registration judge, who received the official archive performs notarial acts only on the documents and papers in the archive.

39.title: Restoration of capacity
paragraphs: Art. 39. (1) The capacity of a notary is restored on his request if it was lost on one of these grounds:
1. deprivation of capacity for a fixed term – after the term expires;
2. an incompatible activity under Art. 9(1), item 1 – after the activity ends.
(2) The request is made to the Council of Notaries within one month of the end of the ground for the loss.
(3) The restoration is noted in the register of the Notary Chamber under Art. 14.
(4) The person who received the notary's official archive must hand it back with an inventory after the restoration.

40.title: Powers of the assistant notary
paragraphs: Art. 40. (1) The assistant notary may perform, on the notary's instructions, all acts within the notary's competence, except:
1. acts that create, transfer, change or end real rights in real estate;
2. acts that recognise ownership or limited real rights in real estate;
3. notarial wills and acts revoking a notarial will;
4. acts that create or delete mortgages.
(2) The assistant notary uses the notary's official archive and seal and adds the word "assistant" to his signature.
(3) The notary is jointly liable with the assistant notary for damage caused by the assistant's culpable non-performance of duties.
(4) In the absence of special rules, the rules for notaries apply to the assistant notary.
(5) The relations between the notary and the assistant notary are governed by a contract.

41.title: Acquisition of capacity (assistant notary)
paragraphs: Art. 41. (1) A notary may name one assistant notary among the persons who meet the requirements for a notary, regardless of their age and experience.

(2) The Minister of Justice issues an order for the entry of the assistant notary in the register of the Notary Chamber on the notary's written application, countersigned by the candidate. The documents under Art. 11(2) are attached. The application may state a term.
(3) The entry in the register is made under Art. 14, 15 and 16.

42.title: Loss of capacity (assistant notary)
paragraphs: Art. 42. (1) The assistant notary loses capacity:
1. on his written request to the notary;
2. on his or the notary's death or placement under judicial disability;
3. when an obstacle under Art. 8 or an incompatibility under Art. 9 arises;
4. on the notary's written request to the Council of Notaries;
5. when the term set by the notary expires, and when the notary is deleted from the register.
(2) The assistant notary is deleted from the register of its own motion or on the notary's request, by noting the ground under para. 1.
(3) The assistant notary loses capacity with the deletion, except in the cases of para. 1, items 2 and 5.

43.title: Competence
paragraphs: Art. 43. (Repealed.)

44.title: Acquisition of capacity
paragraphs: Art. 44. (Repealed.)

45.title: Loss of capacity
paragraphs: Art. 45. (Repealed.)

46.title: Substitution of a notary by an assistant notary
paragraphs: Art. 46. (1) When the notary is absent or unable to perform his functions, he may be substituted by an assistant notary who has the experience under Art. 8(1), item 3 and has passed an exam. In this case the assistant notary performs alone all acts within the notary's competence and adds the words "substituting" to his signature.

(2) The notary and the candidate submit a written application to the Minister of Justice, with the documents under Art. 11(2) for a first entry, and the same documents and the order under para. 5, first sentence, for a later entry. The application states the term of the substitution, which may not exceed two years from the entry in the register.
(3) The candidate takes an exam only for the first term of substitution, under conditions and a procedure set by an ordinance of the Minister of Justice after agreement with the Council of Notaries.
(4) The exam is held by a commission of a representative of the Ministry of Justice, one notary and one inspector-notary named by the Council of Notaries.

(5) The commission presents the protocol with the result to the Minister of Justice, who within 7 days issues an order for entry in the register. An order for a later entry is issued within 7 days of the application under para. 2.
(6) The order under para. 5 is announced to the candidate and the Council of Notaries and may be appealed before the competent administrative court.
(7) The substitution is entered in the register; Art. 41 and 42 apply accordingly.
(8) The Ministry of Justice collects a state fee for the exam set by a tariff approved by the Council of Ministers.

47.title: Substitution of a notary by another notary
paragraphs: Art. 47. (1) A notary may be substituted by another notary of the same district. Their relations are governed by a contract.
(2) The substituting notary uses the archive of the substituted notary, puts his own signature and seal on the certified document and notes the fact of substitution.
(3) If the location of the substituted notary's archive changes during the substitution, Art. 29 applies.
(4) The term of the substitution may not exceed two years from the conclusion of the contract.

48.title: Substitution of a notary by the registration judge
paragraphs: Art. 48. (1) When the notary is absent or unable to perform his functions and nobody in the district substitutes him, he must inform the registration judge, who substitutes him during that time for urgent notarial acts. Art. 47(2) applies accordingly.

(2) If the notary did not provide access to the archive needed for the substitution, the president of the district court, at the request of an interested person, orders entry into the notary office, opening of the necessary archive and performance of the notarial act by the registration judge.

49.title: Official secrecy
paragraphs: Art. 49. The notary's employees must keep the official secret under the conditions set for the notary.

50.title: Delivery of notices and papers
paragraphs: Art. 50. The notary may instruct a specific employee of the notary office to deliver notices and papers under the conditions and procedure of Art. 37–58 of the Civil Procedure Code.

51.title: Statute
paragraphs: Art. 51. The Notary Chamber adopts a statute on its organisation and activity.

52.title: Bodies and representation
paragraphs: Art. 52. (1) The bodies of the Notary Chamber are the general meeting, the Council of Notaries, the control board and the disciplinary commission.
(2) The Notary Chamber is represented by the chair of the Council of Notaries and, in his absence, by his deputies in order of seniority.

53.title: Property
paragraphs: Art. 53. (1) The property of the Notary Chamber consists of:
1. compulsory entry, annual and additional contributions of its members;
2. fees for services;
3. gifts and bequests;
4. other sources.
(2) The Notary Chamber collects fees for entries in its register. The fees are set by a tariff approved by the Council of Ministers.

54.title: Composition
paragraphs: Art. 54. (1) The general meeting consists of all members of the Notary Chamber.
(2) The general meeting is regular or extraordinary.

55.title: Convening
paragraphs: Art. 55. (1) The regular general meeting is convened every year on the last Saturday and Sunday of February.
(2) The Council of Notaries convenes the general meeting by publishing a notice in the State Gazette at least two months before the date. The invitation contains the agenda.
(3) If within 20 days of the publication at least 1/10 of the members ask for an item to be added, the Council of Notaries must publish an addition to the agenda at least 7 days before the meeting.

56.title: Quorum and representation
paragraphs: Art. 56. (1) The general meeting is held if 2/3 of the members are present in person or represented. Without a quorum, the meeting is postponed by one hour and held whatever the number of members present.

(2) Members vote personally or through an agent who is a notary or an assistant notary. The power must be in writing. One agent may represent only one member. The power is presented to the chair of the Council of Notaries or to the administrative secretary before the meeting opens.

57.title: Competence of the general meeting
paragraphs: Art. 57. The general meeting:
1. adopts the statute of the Notary Chamber;
2. elects for 3 years and releases the chair and the members of the Council of Notaries, of the control board and of the disciplinary commission, and sets their number and remuneration;
3. sets the minimum and maximum sum insured under Art. 30(1);
4. decides on group insurance;
5. creates a guarantee fund for compensation of risks not covered by the compulsory insurance or under expired insurance, and decides on other funds;
6. sets the compulsory entry and annual contributions;
7. decides on additional contributions;
8. discusses and adopts the budget of the Chamber;
9. decides on claims of the Chamber against members of its bodies or releases them from liability;
10. decides on the acquisition and disposal of real estate and real rights in it;
11. decides on other matters provided for in the statute.

58.title: Decisions of the general meeting
paragraphs: Art. 58. (1) The general meeting decides by a majority of more than half of the members present. Decisions under Art. 57, items 1, 2 and 7 need more than 2/3 of the members present.
(2) When an election under Art. 57, item 2 goes to a further round, the candidates with the most votes are elected. In a tie, the candidate with longer legal experience under Art. 8(2) is elected.
(3) No decisions may be taken on matters not on the agenda, except the release of members of the bodies and the election of new members in their place.

59.title: Extraordinary general meeting
paragraphs: Art. 59. (1) An extraordinary general meeting is convened by the Council of Notaries, the control board or the Minister of Justice with an agenda set by them.

(2) The Council of Notaries must convene an extraordinary meeting on a written request of 1/10 of the members stating the agenda. If it does not do so within 14 days, the members who made the request convene it.
(3) Art. 55 and 56 apply accordingly.

60.title: Appeal of decisions
paragraphs: Art. 60. (1) Decisions of the general meeting may be appealed before the Supreme Administrative Court within 7 days of the decision.
(2) Any member may join the appeal and support it, also if the appellant withdraws it.
(3) The Minister of Justice may also appeal decisions of the general meeting if they affect a state interest.

61.title: Enforcement
paragraphs: Art. 61. For sums due under a decision of the general meeting, the Notary Chamber may ask for an order for payment under Art. 410(1) of the Civil Procedure Code, regardless of the amount.

62.title: Composition of the Council of Notaries
paragraphs: Art. 62. (1) The Council of Notaries is elected with at least five full and two substitute members; the chair and his deputy are elected from the full members.
(2) In a larger council, two deputy chairs are elected from the full members.
(3) A member of the Notary Chamber may be elected to the Council if he:
1. has at least two years of experience as a notary;
2. has not been elected to this body for more than two consecutive terms.
(4) Members who are prevented or who left are replaced by the substitute members in order of seniority until the obstacle ends or the term ends.
(5) Substitute members replace the chair and his deputies only as members of the Council.

63.title: Meetings of the Council of Notaries
paragraphs: Art. 63. (1) The chair convenes the Council of Notaries in regular session at least once a month.

(2) The chair must convene an extraordinary session on a written request of 1/3 of the full members stating the agenda. If he does not do so within 7 days, the members who made the request convene it.
(3) The Minister of Justice may also convene an extraordinary session with an agenda set by him.

64.title: Quorum
paragraphs: Art. 64. A session of the Council of Notaries is valid if 2/3 of its members are present.

65.title: Competence of the Council of Notaries
paragraphs: Art. 65. (1) The Council of Notaries:
1. directs the work of the Notary Chamber;
2. convenes the general meeting, executes its decisions and reports to it;
3. elects the deputy chairs;
4. sets the staff and the administrative secretary of the Chamber;
5. organises the keeping of the register, decides on entries, notes and deletions in it, and takes the mandatory steps when a notary loses his rights;
6. names the notary who takes part in the competition commission;
7. (Repealed.)

8. supervises the performance of the duties of notaries and assistant notaries, starts disciplinary proceedings against them and takes part in them through its representatives in the cases provided for;
9. directs and carries out the professional training of notaries, their assistants and employees, and protects their professional rights;
10. performs all duties that the law, the statute or the general meeting do not assign to another body.
(2) The Council of Notaries informs the Minister of Justice of the results of the checks under para. 1, item 8.

66.title: Decisions of the Council of Notaries
paragraphs: Art. 66. (1) The Council of Notaries decides by a majority of more than half of the full members present; substitute members present have an advisory vote only, unless they replace full members. In a tie, the chair has the casting vote.
(2) A decision may also be taken in writing without a meeting if all voting members agree and sign it.

67.title: Chair of the Council of Notaries
paragraphs: Art. 67. (1) The chair organises, directs and is responsible for the whole activity of the Council.
(2) The chair:
1. appoints the administrative secretary, the employees and the support staff of the Chamber;
2. manages the property of the Chamber;
3. executes the budget of the Chamber.

68.title: Administrative secretary
paragraphs: Art. 68. (1) The administrative secretary:
1. directs the financial and economic activity;
2. coordinates the support bodies;
3. organises the sessions of the Council of Notaries, prepares the materials and directs the execution of its decisions;
4. directs the employees and the support staff and provides the technical and administrative support for the whole activity of the Chamber.
(2) The administrative secretary need not be a member of the Notary Chamber.

69.title: Composition of the control board
paragraphs: Art. 69. (1) The control board has at least three members.
(2) A member of the Notary Chamber may be elected to the control board if he:
1. has at least two years of experience as a notary;
2. has not been elected to this body for more than two consecutive terms.

70.title: Competence of the control board
paragraphs: Art. 70. (1) The control board controls the financial and economic activity of the Notary Chamber and reports to the general meeting.

(2) When it finds breaches of the law, the statute or the decisions of the general meeting or of the Council of Notaries, the control board prepares a report and submits it to the Council of Notaries or to the general meeting.
(3) Members of the control board may take part in the sessions of the Council of Notaries.

71.title: Composition of the disciplinary commission
paragraphs: Art. 71. (1) The disciplinary commission has at least six members.
(2) A member of the Notary Chamber may be elected to the disciplinary commission if he:
1. has at least two years of experience as a notary;
2. has not been elected to this body for more than two consecutive terms.

72.title: Competence of the disciplinary commission
paragraphs: Art. 72. The disciplinary commission hears and decides disciplinary cases against notaries and assistant notaries under the procedure of the law.

73.title: Liability
paragraphs: Art. 73. (1) The notary is liable for the damage caused by culpable non-performance of his duties under the Obligations and Contracts Act, but not more than the certified material interest.
(2) The state is not liable for the notary's acts.

74.title: Disciplinary offences
paragraphs: Art. 74. (1) The notary and the assistant notary bear disciplinary liability for culpable non-performance of their duties under the law and the statute of the Notary Chamber.
(2) (Repealed.)

75.title: Disciplinary penalties
paragraphs: Art. 75. (1) The disciplinary penalties are:
1. reprimand;
2. a fine of 1,000 to 5,000 leva;
3. a warning of deprivation of capacity;
4. deprivation of capacity for 3 months to 5 years.
(2) The fine under para. 1, item 2 is collected for the Notary Chamber.

76.title: Limitation of disciplinary liability
paragraphs: Art. 76. (1) Disciplinary liability is extinguished 6 months after the offence is discovered, and in any case two years after it was committed.

(2) The offence is discovered when the body under Art. 77(1) learns of it. If it learns of it through a complaint or a signal, the body must start disciplinary proceedings within three months if it finds a disciplinary offence.

77.title: Start of disciplinary proceedings
paragraphs: Art. 77. (1) Disciplinary proceedings start on a proposal of the Minister of Justice or of its own motion by decision of the Council of Notaries.
(2) The body that started the proceedings informs the notary, who may give explanations within 7 days.
(3) After the term under para. 2, the Council of Notaries sends the materials to the chair of the disciplinary commission.
(4) The chair of the disciplinary commission names a chair and two members of the panel that hears the case.

78.title: Hearing of a disciplinary case
paragraphs: Art. 78. (1) The chair of the panel schedules a hearing and invites the notary, a representative of the Council of Notaries and a representative of the Minister of Justice when the proceedings started on his request. The notary may have a lawyer.
(2) The hearings of the disciplinary commission are closed.
(3) All evidence relevant to the case is admitted.

79.title: Decision
paragraphs: Art. 79. (1) The commission decides the case by a reasoned decision.
(2) The decision is taken after secret deliberation by a majority of the panel.
(3) A decision imposing the penalty under Art. 75(1), item 4 needs a majority of two thirds of the members of the disciplinary commission. Without this majority, the decision is taken under para. 2.
(4) The commission hears and decides the case within one month of its assignment.

(5) The decision is communicated to the notary, the Council of Notaries and the Minister of Justice under the Civil Procedure Code. The Minister names by order the official who certifies delivery or receipt.

80.title: Appeal and entry into force of the decision
paragraphs: Art. 80. (1) The notary, the Council of Notaries and the Minister of Justice may appeal the decision of the disciplinary commission before the Supreme Court of Cassation within 14 days of its communication.
(2) The Minister of Justice may appeal also when the proceedings started by decision of the Council of Notaries.
(3) The Supreme Court of Cassation hears the appeal on the merits in a panel of three judges.

81.title: General rule
paragraphs: Art. 81. A person who is not a notary may perform notarial functions only as far as the law provides.

82.title: Judicial bodies
paragraphs: Art. 82. (1) When there is no notary in the district, the notarial acts are performed by the registration judge at the district court.
(2) When there is a notary, the registration judge performs notarial acts only on the documents in the archive of the registry office, and notarial acts when substituting a notary.

83.title: Local administration bodies
paragraphs: Art. 83. (1) When the settlement has no notary or district court, the mayor of a settlement that is not a municipal centre – and in a municipal centre, the mayor, the deputy mayor, the municipal secretary and the mayor's deputy – certify signatures on private documents that are unilateral acts and are not subject to entry, the signature and content of a power of attorney under Art. 37 of the Obligations and Contracts Act, and the correctness of copies and extracts of documents and papers.
(2) The persons under para. 1 may not certify signatures on private documents in the cases of Art. 15(1), Art. 129(2) and Art. 137(6) of the Commerce Act.

84.title: Bulgarian diplomatic and consular officers
paragraphs: Art. 84. (1) Bulgarian consular officers abroad, following the relevant rules of the Civil Procedure Code and if the document is in Bulgarian, may:
1. certify the date, content and signatures of private documents that are not subject to entry and are presented by Bulgarian or foreign citizens;
2. certify the correctness of copies and extracts of documents presented by Bulgarian citizens;
3. make notarial wills of Bulgarian citizens.
(2) The date, content and signature of a private document not subject to entry and presented by a foreign citizen are certified only if the document is to take effect in Bulgaria.

85.title: Grounds and amount of fees
paragraphs: Art. 85. (1) Notarial fees are collected for:
1. notarial acts;
2. other acts performed by a notary.
(2) The same fee is collected for the same notarial act performed by a notary and by a state body.
(3) The amounts of the notarial fees are set by a tariff adopted by the Council of Ministers on a proposal of the Minister of Justice after agreement with the Notary Chamber.

86.title: Payment of fees
paragraphs: Art. 86. Notarial fees are revenue of:
1. the notary in whose official archive the act is recorded;
2. the municipal budget – for notarial acts by local administration bodies;
3. the state budget – for notarial acts by other bodies, including a registration judge substituting a notary.

87.title: Persons liable
paragraphs: Art. 87. Notarial fees are owed by the person whose request a notary or another body with notarial functions considered. Several liable persons are jointly liable.

88.title: When fees are due
paragraphs: Art. 88. (1) Notarial fees are due when the requested act is performed; fees for circumstantial verifications are due when the request is filed.
(2) The notary has the right to ask for part of the fee in advance.

89.title: Collection of fees
paragraphs: Art. 89. (1) For the collection of notarial fees a bill is prepared in two or more identical copies signed by the notary; one copy is handed to the liable person.

(2) The bill states the provisions under which the fees are due, the certified material interest or the time spent for a proportional fee, the amounts of the fees and additional costs, the advance received and the consequences of non-payment.
(3) For notarial fees due and unpaid, the notary may ask for an order for payment under Art. 410(1) of the Civil Procedure Code, regardless of the amount.
(4) When the material interest was set wrongly and fees were collected, the fees actually due are collected on a bill signed by the notary and prepared within 7 days of discovering the error.

90.title: Ordinary fees
paragraphs: Art. 90. (1) Ordinary notarial fees are collected only for acts expressly listed in the tariff and do not depend on the material interest or the time spent.

(2) An ordinary fee is due for the notarial certification of the content of a document that, under the Commerce Act or the Special Pledges Act, is made at the same time as the certification of its signatures.

91.title: Proportional fees
paragraphs: Art. 91. Proportional notarial fees are collected according to the certified material interest or the time spent, and have a set minimum.

92.title: Fees according to the material interest
paragraphs: Art. 92. (1) The percentage of the proportional fee decreases as the material interest increases, and the fee may not exceed a set maximum.
(2) For certain kinds of certification the tariff may provide a reduced or an increased fee.

93.title: Fees according to the time spent
paragraphs: Art. 93. (1) Fees according to the time spent are due only to notaries and are paid for:
1. oral and written consultations;
2. mediation to clarify the will of the parties;
3. inquiries, obtaining documents, papers and others.
(2) No fee is due for oral consultations given in connection with another charged act.

94.title: Fees for drafting and checking documents
paragraphs: Art. 94. (1) Fees for drafting and checking documents are due only to notaries.
(2) For drafting a notarial deed or another document, the fee for the certification is collected.
(3) For checking a draft document without certifying it, half of the certification fee is collected. If the same notary certifies the same document within one month, only the other half is collected.

95.title: Additional fee
paragraphs: Art. 95. (1) An additional notarial fee is due for acts performed at the applicant's request outside the notary office, out of working hours, or on rest days and holidays.
(2) The fee under para. 1 is due in a total amount of half of the certification fee.

96.title: Transactions with real rights
paragraphs: Art. 96. (1) In the transfer and certification of ownership of things, the certified material interest is:
1. the market price of the thing;
2. the market price of the more valuable thing – in an exchange;
3. the market price of all shares – in a voluntary partition.
(2) In the creation or transfer of other real rights, the certified material interest is:
1. for a building right – 90 per cent of the market price of the land, or of the part of it on which the right is created or transferred;
2. for the creation of a right of use – the market rent for the whole term of use, and if no term is set – for 3 years.
(3) When the assessment under § 2 and the certified material interest differ, the fee is collected on the higher of the two.

97.title: Special cases
paragraphs: Art. 97. (1) The certified material interest is:
1. in a transaction with a motor vehicle – the value for which it is insured;
2. in a transaction with a commercial enterprise – the book value of the fixed assets of the enterprise for the past quarter;
3. in the founding of a commercial company – the capital;
4. in the sale of an inheritance – the market price of the real estate in the inheritance;
5. in the execution of wills – the market price of the property bequeathed;
6. in the management of property – the monthly income from the property;
7. in a transaction on a money claim – the nominal value of the claim, and for periodic payments – the total of the payments for the whole term, and if no term is set – for 3 years.
(2) In changes and additions to transactions and documents, the certified material interest is only that of the changes.
(3) In transactions for value, the certified material interest is the contract price, if it is higher than the value under this section.

25а.title: Special bank account of the notary
paragraphs: Art. 25a. (1) In acts that create, transfer, change or end real rights in real estate, the sum due under the transaction may be transferred or deposited into a special bank account in the name of the notary.
(2) The conditions for depositing sums into the notary's special account and for payment orders by the notary are set in a written agreement between the notary and the parties to the transaction.
(3) No enforcement for the notary's debts is allowed against the money in the special bank account.

28а.title: Notarial registers and books
paragraphs: Art. 28a. (1) Every notary keeps:
1. a general register;
2. an alphabetical index;
3. a register for the deposit, return and announcement of holographic wills and for the acceptance and return of documents and papers deposited for safekeeping;
4. a book formed of the notarial and other acts and documents subject to entry, and of the marriage contracts under Art. 39 of the Family Code;
5. a book formed of notarial wills and acts revoking wills;
6. a book of notarial invitations, protests, declaratory protocols and copies of documents with certified content;
7. a delivery book.
(2) The general register and the books under para. 1, items 6 and 7 are kept for 10 years; after that they are destroyed after agreement with the respective state archive.

(3) The alphabetical index, the register under para. 1, item 3 and the books under para. 1, items 4 and 5 are kept for 100 years; after that they are handed over for permanent storage to the respective state archive.

(4) Information from notarial case files is given only to the parties, their successors and their representatives by law or by authorisation. An agent who is not a lawyer must be authorised expressly by a notarially certified power of attorney.

28б.title: Information system
paragraphs: Art. 28b. An information system is established at the Notary Chamber, containing a database that is part of the notary's official archive. The right of access to the system and the data entered are set by the ordinance under Art. 28(1).

34а.title: Association of notaries
paragraphs: Art. 34a. Notaries may associate and act together as a civil partnership under Art. 357–364 of the Obligations and Contracts Act. In these cases each notary keeps a separate archive.

34б.title: Transfer of a notary
paragraphs: Art. 34b. (1) A notary may be transferred for important reasons to another district on a reasoned application to the Minister of Justice, when a place under Art. 10 is open.

(2) Important reasons are circumstances that arose independently of the notary's will after he acquired capacity. They may concern his health, family situation and others that in all cases lead to full or partial impossibility to perform notarial functions in his current district.
(3) Two notaries may exchange their districts for important reasons and by agreement. In this case they file a joint application under para. 1.

(4) The Minister of Justice decides within 14 days of the application, after agreement with the Notary Chamber. The order is communicated to the notary, the Council of Notaries and the Supreme Administrative Prosecutor's Office under Art. 18a(10) of the Administrative Procedure Code.

(5) The Council of Notaries may appeal the transfer order when the transfer breached the law. The notary may appeal a refusal. The appeal goes to the competent administrative court under the Administrative Procedure Code.
(6) On a transfer, Art. 13, 14, 16, 36 and 38 apply.
(7) On an exchange under para. 3, each notary must accept the official archive of the other.

80а.title: Expiry of disciplinary penalties
paragraphs: Art. 80a. A disciplinary penalty is deleted when the following time has passed since it was imposed:
1. one year – for the penalty under Art. 75(1), item 1;
2. two years from the payment or enforced collection of the fine under Art. 75(1), item 2;
3. three years from the penalty under Art. 75(1), item 3;
4. five years from the end of the term of the penalty under Art. 75(1), item 4.

80б.title: Form of control
paragraphs: Art. 80b. (1) The Minister of Justice controls the activity of every notary for compliance with the law and the statute of the Notary Chamber. The Minister assigns joint inspections to inspectors of the Inspectorate of the Minister of Justice under the Judiciary Act and to inspector-notaries under Art. 80c(4).
(2) An inspection is ordered by the Minister of Justice of his own motion, on a signal or complaint of an interested person, or on a proposal of the Council of Notaries. The order cannot be appealed.
(3) A protocol records the findings of the inspection; a copy goes to the Council of Notaries.

80в.title: Status of inspector-notaries
paragraphs: Art. 80c. (1) (Repealed.)
(2) Members of the Notary Chamber with more than 10 years of legal experience, of which three as a notary, are proposed as inspector-notaries.

(3) Inspector-notaries are elected by the general meeting of the respective notarial college for three years, by a majority of more than half of the members present. There are at least 10 inspector-notaries in total.
(4) After the election the Council of Notaries prepares the list of inspector-notaries and presents it to the Minister of Justice.
§ 1. "Notarial fee" within the meaning of this Act is the remuneration paid to a notary for the service performed.

§ 2. The market price is the price that could be obtained in ordinary market relations, taking into account the nature of the object and all factors that affect the price in a sale or a lease. The assessment is made under Art. 33 of the Local Taxes and Fees Act.
